title: RADIAN: Regime-Adaptive Dilated Inter-Attention Network for Non-Stationary Financial Time-Series Forecasting
content: Financial forecasting is challenged by non-stationarity, volatility clustering, and regime transitions that induce distribution shifts. Conventional neural architectures often rely on shared decoder mappings that inadequately capture regime-dependent dynamics. We introduce RADIAN (Regime-Adaptive Dilated Inter-Attention Network), which preserves regime-agnostic temporal and cross-variable encoders while applying causal regime conditioning only in gated fusion and decoding. A deterministic four-dimensional regime vector computed from normalized one-step target returns guides a regime-aware gated mixture-of-experts directional head, path-based trajectory construction, and residual correction; SafeFeatureRevIN preserves sample-specific scale during normalization and reconstruction. We evaluate RADIAN on nine hourly financial datasets across asset classes against eight baselines under a fixed protocol with three seeds. RADIAN achieves the lowest mean test MAE, improving by 0.6704% on average over the strongest per-dataset baseline, and the lowest RMSE on all nine datasets and lowest MSE/MAE on eight. RMSE improvement averages 0.41% (median 0.36%), and mean directional accuracy reaches 51.279% versus 50.950% for the next-best model average. Paired tests show large effect sizes, with Benjamini-Hochberg-corrected significance on two datasets. Ablations confirm decoder-side regime conditioning: removing path decoding raises RMSE by up to 2.55%, and replacing gated fusion reduces directional accuracy by up to 1.15 percentage points. RADIAN attains an aggregated test RMSE of 94.1048 with 516,425 parameters and processes batches of 64 in 24.7172 ms versus 83.7451 ms for ModernTCN. These findings support decoder-centric causal regime conditioning for accurate, efficient financial forecasting under heterogeneous market conditions.
